i-reference/studies/update-a-scenario.md): Change a study's identity or its exposure, but not both in one call. **Send `mode` on i
ts own.** Identity and exposure are separate operations upstream, and applying them in sequence could leave the study live in a mo
de you did not ask for.\n- [List a scenario's sessions](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/studies/list-a-scenarios-sessions.md
): What visitors did, as summaries. Project members only: this route is deliberately absent from the guest allowlist, so a share-l
ink visitor can never read other visitors' sessions.\n- [Get a session transcript](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/studies/g
et-a-session-transcript.md): The projected transcript, paged. Tool payloads and blobs are dropped, and the stored blob URL is neve
r returned.\n- [Set the guest-execution caps](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/studies/set-the-guest-execution-caps.md): The
spend dial for anonymous visitors. A FULL REPLACEMENT. Send every field. These caps only mean something as a set, and a partial up
date that raised one while leaving another stale would produce a combination nobody chose.\n- [Rotate the share link](https://docs
.mcpjam.com/api-reference/studies/rotate-the-share-link.md): Mints a new share link and stops the old URL from granting access. Ev
eryone you shared it with needs the new one.\n- [Invite a member](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/studies/invite-a-member.md
): Upsert by email, so re-inviting somebody is not an error. Only meaningful while `mode` is `invited_only`.\n- [Remove a member](
https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/studies/remove-a-member.md): Removal NARROWS access, so it bumps `accessVersion` and cuts of
f any session that member already had: it takes effect at once rather than at expiry.\n- [Point a scenario at a different environm
ent](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/studies/point-a-scenario-at-a-different-environment.md): Keeps the study's LINK, its me
mbers and its session history while changing what visitors actually reach. The alternative, unpublish and republish, mints a new l
ink, which means re-sharing it with everyone.\n- [Session metrics](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/studies/session-metrics.m
d): Volumes, completion and feedback rates over the study's sessions.\n- [Usage breakdown](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/s
tudies/usage-breakdown.md): Which models, tools and servers the study's sessions used.\n- [Current window signals](https://docs.mc
pjam.com/api-reference/studies/current-window-signals.md): What the miner extracted from the current window, and where you get the
window id the insights read takes.\n- [List scenario findings](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/studies/list-scenario-findin
gs.md): Every finding raised over this study's windows, dismissed ones included: dismissal is a state on the finding, not a deleti
on.\n- [Read a window's insights](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/studies/read-a-windows-insights.md): Poll this after reque
sting a generation.\n- [Request insights for the current window](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/studies/request-insights-fo
r-the-current-window.md): **No credits are consumed**: the model cost is on MCPJam. Runs a model over the study's current window a
nd draws on the organization's `insightsPerDay` ledger, which counts REQUESTS and is SHARED with eval-run and swarm run insights,
so a request here takes one from there.\n- [Cancel a window's generation](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/studies/cancel-a-w
indows-generation.md): Releases a generation that is stuck `pending`. Idempotent against an already-finished one.\n- [Dismiss a fi
nding](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/studies/dismiss-a-finding.md): Keyed on the finding's stable remediation id, so the s
ame problem stays dismissed when insights regenerate. Bodyless: the path names the finding.\n- [Restore a dismissed finding](https
://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/studies/restore-a-dismissed-finding.md): Undoes a dismissal. Bodyless: the path names the finding
.\n- [Create (or revive) a relay tunnel for a named project server](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/tunnels/create-or-revive
-a-relay-tunnel-for-a-named-project-server.md): Registers a server record named `name` if missing, mints a relay tunnel grant for
it, and **persists the tunnel bearer URL (including the plaintext `?k=` secret) onto the server record's `url`** so evals and stud
ies can target the tunnel like any remote server. **Every call rotates the secret, revok…\n- [Revoke a tunnel's live grant](https:
//docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/tunnels/revoke-a-tunnels-live-grant.md): Revokes the grant: the public URL stops working immediate
ly and any live tunnel session is disconnected. The server record, including its now-dead `url`, is intentionally left untouched,
so the next create revives the tunnel with the same slug.\n- [Run one headless agent turn](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/a
gent/run-one-headless-agent-turn.md): Runs ONE assistant turn over the supplied message history and responds synchronously with th
e final assistant text, the operations it invoked, references to any resources it created, and any actions awaiting human approval
.\n- [Connect an MCP server](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/server-connections/connect-an-mcp-server.md): Starts a connecti
on request for an MCP server URL. Discovery, browser consent, and validation happen asynchronously; poll the returned `connectionR
equestId` until the status is terminal. When the next step belongs to a person, the response carries a `handoffUrl` to open.\n- [G
et a connection request](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/server-connections/get-a-connection-request.md): Current state of o
ne connection request. Metered on its own poll budget rather than the shared per-caller one, so polling on a short interval is exp
ected and will not spend the budget your other calls need. A 429 here means the poll interval itself is too fast; honour Retry-Aft
er.\n- [Cancel a connection request](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/server-connections/cancel-a-connection-request.md): Sto
ps a request and invalidates its handoff link. Cancelling an already-terminal request is a no-op.\n- [Retry validation](https://do
cs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/server-connections/retry-validation.md): Re-arms a stalled validation immediately instead of waiting o
ut its backoff. Does not revive a terminal request: after `failed`, `expired`, or `cancelled`, start a new one.\n- [List personas]
(https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarms/list-personas.md): The project's personas, newest first. Archived personas are exclu
ded.\n- [Create a persona](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarms/create-a-persona.md): Creates one persona. To draft severa
l with a model first, use `POST /projects/{projectId}/personas/generate`: that route persists nothing.\n- [Get a persona](https://
docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarms/get-a-persona.md): A persona that lives in a DIFFERENT project answers 404, never 403: the ro
ute is not an existence oracle for a project you cannot see.\n- [Delete a persona](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarms/de
lete-a-persona.md): Refused with 409 while goals still reference this persona: deleting it would strand them.\n- [Update a persona
](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarms/update-a-persona.md): Partial update. Goals reference the persona by id, so renamin
g one does not disturb anything pointing at it.\n- [Draft personas with a model](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarms/draf
t-personas-with-a-model.md): Returns DRAFTS and persists nothing; save the ones you want with the create routes. There is no idemp
otency key, and retries return different drafts.\n- [Draft journeys for a persona](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarms/dr
aft-journeys-for-a-persona.md): Returns DRAFTS and persists nothing. See `POST /projects/{projectId}/personas/generate` for why, a
nd for the quota this counts against.\n- [Get a journey](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarms/get-a-journey.md)\n- [Archiv
e a journey](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarms/archive-a-journey.md): ARCHIVES rather than deletes, and the response sa
ys so. Existing runs keep pointing at the definition they executed, so their history stays readable.\n- [Update a journey](https:/
/docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarms/update-a-journey.md): Editing a goal never disturbs a run already under way: a run pins its
